title: Symmetric difference by a singleton toggles a Walsh character
statement:
Let $S\subseteq[n]$, let $i\in[n]$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. Then the Walsh--Fourier character indexed by the symmetric difference $S\mathbin{\triangle}\{i\}$ satisfies
\[
  \chi_{S\,\triangle\,\{i\}}(x) \;=\; \chi_S(x)\,\sigma(x_i),
\]
where $\sigma$ is the sign encoding $\sigma(x_i)=(-1)^{x_i}$.
hypotheses_covered: x is a point of the Boolean cube {0,1}^n
replaced:
For all $S$, $i$, and $x$ in the Boolean cube,
$\chi_{S \triangle \{i\}}(x) = \chi_S(x)\cdot \mathrm{boolToSign}(x_i)$.
